What packages are allowed in the lake folder? Challenge file (should!) only depend(s) on mathlib.

@Matthew Ballard, sorry to put words in your mouth but I'm having trouble understanding you. I think your question should have been:

My pinned lean-informal Git dependency has an inherited path dependency tfb, which Lake records as .lake/packages/informal/tfb; Palomar rejects all path dependencies under .lake. Is this layout intentionally unsupported even though Challenge.lean imports only Mathlib?

And the answer is then an easy: "yes, that is intentionally unsupported, why would you do that?" :-)

I'm having trouble understanding you

Imagine being my wife. :)

I understand that randos (like me) with rando packages should be excluded, ie white list model.

The question was about where to draw the line. The link was motivation for me. (It is possible the model was mid fix of things and modified the lakefile to point to a local dirty copy of this package. In that case, this is user error! But checking the current main commit it is pointing to a git repo.)

For example, I cannot import verso right? There is certainly an incredible amount of value there especially for exposing AI work to humans in a digestible fashion. So being able to support that as allowed would be nice at some point.

TLDR: what is the white list and what is the process for adding to it?
For the statements, the whitelist is currently Mathlib, CSLib, and (presumably controversially :woman_shrugging:) Tau Ceti.
Do we encourage a separate package for say Verso use?

(In case any cares, my particular use case is a meta program that generates a compliant challenge from any specified theorem. Of I can do I CI dance to get something conforming. And that is fine. I am not requesting an exception. But I am lazy. AI use and all…)
